articles.title: Socceroos and Matildas sue Football Australia over revenue share dispute
articles.summary: Union is pursuing seven-figure sum on behalf of players. Central issue believed to surround FA’s commercial deals. Socceroos and Matildas players have sued Football Australia as part of a multi-million dollar dispute between the governing body and its national team players.
body: AAP understands the players’ union, Professional Footballers Australia (PFA), is pursuing FA for a seven-figure sum on behalf of the players.
The union is expected to argue the revenue share agreement between the governing body and national teams players is not being serviced properly.
The central issue is believed to surround FA’s commercial deals and whether players are getting a fair share of FA revenues.
As part of the existing collective bargaining agreement (CBA), which was signed in 2023, Socceroos and Matildas players take a clip of FA’s national team revenues.

articles.title: Curtain falls on Big Show as Glenn Maxwell retires from T20 international cricket
articles.summary: Explosive batter calls time having amassed 2,897 runs at 28.97. 38-year-old will continue to play franchise cricket. Australian short-form cricket star Glenn Maxwell has retired from the international game.
body: “Post the last one-day game for Victoria, speaking to my teammates and letting them know that was going to be my last game for the state was probably harder than I thought it was going to be – got a little choked up,” Maxwell said on The Final Word podcast.

Maxwell played with Australia at the T20 World Cup in India and Sri Lanka earlier this year and across his career played 130 T20 internationals, scoring 2,897 runs at 28.97 and with a strike rate of 154.42.
He also took 51 wickets and 62 catches and posted a high score of 145 not out, which he scored against Sri Lanka in 2016.

“I’m grateful for the time I was able to play for my country,” he said. “If you had offered me that career when I first walked into the Vic change rooms in 2009-ish, I would have bitten your hand off.

articles.title: Jeers again as home woes continue - Jaissle has big problems at Newcastle
articles.summary: Three months into a four-year contract, the problems are mounting for Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle after his side were booed off the pitch by their own fans following another defeat.
body: If Matthias Jaissle was unsure what Newcastle fans thought of his team's latest error-strewn performance, he certainly knew at full-time after a second defeat by Everton inside a week.
Despite another miserable showing by Jaissle's side, the Toon Army had stuck by the team from start to finish before a chorus of boos echoed around St James' Park at the final whistle.

The frustration and anger from the stands came after a 1-0 defeat which included a goalkeeping howler by Lukas Hornicek, a red card for substitute Jacob Ramsey and another blunt attacking performance.
"Big frustration, big disappointment," said Jaissle after a fourth defeat in six Premier League games.

articles.title: Fifa to share documents on World Cup sell-off plans with council members
articles.summary: Viewings to take place at Fifa’s headquarters in Zurich. No direct response to Uefa’s questions on governance. Fifa will grant its council members access to documents regarding the doomed Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme but has not responded directly to more than 50 questions from Uefa about its…
body: In a letter sent to the Fifa Council by Mattias Grafström, the governing body’s secretary general, members were told material relating to FFE will be released for them to view in person at Fifa’s headquarters in Zurich. They will be allowed only to view the documents, of which the exact nature and scope are unclear, under strict confidentiality protocols. A deadline of 16 November has been set to apply for such visits; eyebrows may be raised in some quarters about the fact this is two days before candidates for the Fifa election next year are required to declare their hand.

Uefa had written to Grafström on 19 October giving Fifa a fortnight to answer a series of questions about FFE, the Folarin Balogun affair, the Fifa peace prize, the organisation’s relations with Donald Trump and other major decisions that have caused controversy in the past 12 months. It had asked for all documents regarding FFE to be made accessible, saying refusal to comply with any of its demands should be “justified individually, with a clear explanation of the specific grounds relied upon”.

articles.title: Lions’ Jack Campbell remains hospitalized after ‘scary’ neck injury but initial signs are positive
articles.summary: Team say they will not release further information. 26-year-old will remain in hospital for time being. The Detroit Lions have said the initial signs for Jack Campbell are “positive” after the linebacker was carted off the field and taken to hospital when he suffered a neck injury during Sunday’s…
body: The 26-year-old was treated for nine minutes on the field after making a tackle during Sunday’s game. Players from both teams were visibly distraught as Campbell received medical attention before he was taken for further treatment at a nearby facility.

“Jack Campbell continues to rest and recover at a local hospital,” the Lions said in a statement on Monday. “Preliminary indications are positive and out of respect for Jack and his family we will not share further information at this time.”

Lions coach Dan Campbell also gave a brief update on the linebacker’s condition on Monday. “It’s positive news on Jack,” said Dan Campbell. “So your prayers are working. Please continue to do that and we’ll leave it at that.”
The Lions coach also paid tribute to the former first-round pick’s contributions to the team.

articles.title: Wake Forest Beats Maryland-Eastern Shore 83-62 in Season Opener
articles.summary: It didn’t always look great, but at the end of night, the Wake Forest Demon Deacons are 1-0 with a 21 point win over the Maryland-Eastern Shore Hawks. 1-0 🎩 pic.twitter.com/CZ1SKHCeok. — Wake Forest Men's Basketball (@WakeMBB) November 3, 2026. The story in this one is Gavin Placide.
body: The story in this one is Gavin Placide. The true freshman was completely dominant in his first real game as a Demon Deacon, finishing with 20 points, 7 rebounds, 2 assists, 2 blocks, and 3 steals. He definitely did not look like a freshman out there, and the Hawks really had no answer for him throughout the game. His brother Gallagher also had a solid first game, finishing with 13 points on 6-10 shooting. The twins helped the Deacs outscore the Hawks 44-22 in the paint and were a major part of a 20-0 2nd half run that sealed the win for Wake Forest. Based on the first game, Wake’s ceiling this season is going to depend heavily upon the play and development of the Placide brothers.

articles.title: No. 1 Gators return to Tampa after NCAA loss, beat No. 14 Miami in opener
articles.summary: Seven months ago, Florida was on the brink of another Sweet 16 appearance, another step toward its quest to repeat as national champion. Benchmark International Arena, filled with the Gator faithful, was set to be the site of another celebration.
body: Isaiah Brown was at the foul line, awarded two free throws that would’ve given Florida a three-point lead with eight seconds remaining in the round of 32 battle. After Brown’s trip to the foul line, the Gators would have a chance to sabotage Iowa’s shot at tying the game with a take foul.

But Brown missed a free throw. Before Florida could foul, Iowa’s Alvaro Folgueiras found room in the corner and drained a 3-pointer to give the Hawkeyes the lead with 4.5 seconds remaining. A last-gasp play call proved futile, and in a matter of moments an NCAA tournament campaign poised to continue came to a crashing halt with a 73-72 loss.
In their return to Tampa Monday night against No. 14 Miami in the Orion180 Tip-Off Classic, the Gators kept things comfortable in a 77-67 win.
In its high-pressure game against Iowa, however, Florida couldn’t escape the chaos of college basketball in March.

articles.title: Gilgeous-Alexander leads Thunder past Cavs, Grizzlies beaten
articles.summary: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander erupted for 43 points as the Oklahoma City Thunder halted their two-game losing streak with a battling 117-112 road victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Monday.
body: Oklahoma City had been rocked after suffering a slew of injuries followed by back-to-back 20-point defeats heading into Monday's showdown with last season's Eastern Conference finalists.
But a sublime performance from two-time reigning NBA Most Valuable Player Gilgeous-Alexander carried the Thunder to a morale-boosting win at Cleveland's Rocket Arena.
Gilgeous-Alexander's 43-point haul came from 14-of-35 shooting from the field with four three-pointers and eight assists.
Oklahoma City, missing three starters in Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace, were also boosted by 20 points from Ajay Mitchell and 12 points from Kenrich Williams.

articles.title: Carragher: Boring Newcastle face a tough season ahead
articles.summary: Jamie Carragher described Newcastle as flat and boring following their defeat to Everton on Monday Night Football and reckons Matthias Jaissle's side faces a difficult season.
body: Thierno Barry's second-half goal earned Everton a 1-0 win at St James' Park and their first away victory in the Premier League this season, as Newcastle were booed off at half-time and full-time following their fourth defeat in five games across all competitions.
Newcastle have slipped to 13th and are now four points above the bottom three, with a trip to lowly Fulham to come on Saturday.

"I think it is going to be a tough season for them," said Sky Sports' Carragher. "I felt tonight [Monday] was actually more important for Newcastle than the cup game [Carabao Cup loss at Everton last week], and it was the other way round for Everton, who are desperate for a trophy.
"But I fear a little bit for Newcastle, I think it could be a long, tough season."

articles.title: Harmer urges England to recall Leach - and stop 'isolating' spinners
articles.summary: South Africa's Simon Harmer said England should take Jack Leach on the Test tour of his homeland this winter as he suggested a lack of spin coaches in county cricket is leaving slow bowlers "isolated".
body: Since Ben Stokes' international retirement in June, England have rejigged the balance of their side with Dan Lawrence's part-time off-spin now supporting four fast bowlers - a policy they could maintain when they play South Africa in three Tests from December 17.

However, Proteas frontline off-spinner Harmer, a county-cricket stalwart with Essex, bagged 14 wickets in three games in the just-completed 2-1 series win at home to Australia, including a 10-wicket match haul in the deciding Test at Cape Town.

Somerset left-arm spinner Leach last played for England two years ago - he does not have a central contract - and national selector Marcus North recently told the Wisden Cricket Weekly podcast that the team were moving in a "different direction."

Harmer, though, told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast Leach, who has 142 wickets in 39 Tests to date an an average of 34.07, "would be his guy" as England prepare to tackle South Africa in Johannesburg, Centurion and Cape Town, live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: No. 1 Florida opens season with convincing victory vs. Miami: Gators show why they deserve No. 1 ranking
articles.summary: Top-ranked Florida returned to where its season came to an end in March and easily handled the No. 14 Hurricanes
body: TAMPA, Fla. -- No. 1 Florida opened the 2026-27 college basketball season with a statement Monday, defeating No. 14 Miami 77-67 behind a huge night from national player of the year candidate Thomas Haugh. The star forward who bypassed the NBA Draft to return for his senior season with the Gators finished with a team-high 19 points and 10 rebounds.

Haugh matched the best 3-point shooting night of his college career against Miami by draining four of his eight shots from beyond the arc. The last time Haugh knocked down four 3-pointers in a game came against Texas Tech in the 2025 Elite Eight. Florida went on to win the national title that year, and the Gators look like this season could produce a similar run.

Seven months ago, Florida lost to Iowa here at Benchmark International Arena in the second round of the NCAA Tournament in one of the most shocking results of the entire season. Haugh, Rueben Chinyelu, Alex Condon, Boogie Fland and Urban Klavžar returned from that team that lost in this arena.
